items.mnemonic_text: A lid across the top, and underneath it two strokes crossing each other and splaying out at the bottom like arms thrown wide. It is a figure with something draped over its shoulders and a pattern brushed right across the chest — marks made on purpose, meant to be read. Marks put there to be read are <radical>writing</radical>.

Look at 馬 side-on: the top box is the head, and those four little legs dashing along the bottom are hooves kicking up dust. Picture that boxy body galloping past you and you're looking at a <radical>horse</radical>.
Those four little dots are the glowing embers left at the bottom of a campfire pit, each one a tiny tongue of flame licking up from underneath — the <radical>fire</radical> burning along the bottom.

Picture a tall candle standing upright, with a tiny flame flickering off each side of the wick — that thin vertical stroke and its two little side dashes. This candle is the one you light when you're pouring your whole heart into a wish, so 忄is the <radical>heart</radical>, squeezed slim and standing off to the left.
items.description: Both are three strokes down the left edge. 忄 hangs a short dash on each side of one long vertical. 氵 has no vertical at all — just three separate slanting drops stacked downward.

items.mnemonic_text: The long diagonal slash is a halberd's shaft, propped against a gate at an angle no guard would choose; the hooked stroke off it is the crescent blade, and the lone dot above is where a passing guard's scarf snagged on the tip. The scarf yanks tight, the whole thing topples clattering — a <radical>halberd</radical>.

The big figure standing with both arms flung wide suddenly sprouts a stray fleck up by its shoulder, and it snaps at that one spot again and again, never quite reaching it. It spins in a tight, undignified circle chasing its own shoulder, because no <radical>dog</radical> has ever caught its own tail either.
items.description: 大 (big) is just the figure with arms out, no extra mark anywhere. 太 (thick / fat) adds its dot low down, between the legs, like a belly bulge. 犬 adds its dot high up, by the shoulder, like the flea it keeps snapping at — the dot's height is the only difference between all three.

items.mnemonic_text: An outer frame, and set inside it another box with a bar ruled across — a mask hung on a wall, with the flat plane of the cheeks around it and the eyes cut into the middle. It shows you nothing of whoever is behind it. All you get is the front of the thing, its <radical>face</radical>.

Picture a garden trellis with a single vine climbing up it, and hanging from that vine is one fat, round moon that's caught the twilight — the whole thing glowing that impossible shade between the sky and the sea, <radical>blue-green</radical>.

A short jagged stroke splits off at the top like a bone that has already cracked, and the rest of the frame sags underneath it, snapped clean through at the joint. Nothing about it can be set or straightened again, just plain <radical>death / bad luck</radical> drooping off the corner of the shape.
items.description: This shape almost always sits on the left side of a kanji as a component, quietly signaling that the meaning has to do with dying, decay, or misfortune rather than carrying a pronunciation of its own.

items.mnemonic_text: A net stretched flat across the top, and underneath it a shell — the old money, before coins. You spread the net, you sweep the shells in, and you hand them over the counter for whatever was on the shelf. Shells going out under a net is what it looks like to <radical>buy</radical> something.

See that little cross-stroke on top as a coat hanger's hook, and the wide, splayed strokes hanging below it as the sleeves and hem draping down — the whole shape is a shirt hung up to dry, a piece of <radical>clothing</radical>.

Picture a single log standing upright, with two sparks flicking off its sides — that's exactly what 火 looks like. Those sparks jumping into the air tell you the whole thing is on <radical>fire</radical>.

Look at 川 and you're standing on a bank watching three long streams of water pour down the page side by side, the outer two bending with the current. Those three vertical channels flowing together are a <radical>river</radical>.

A cross of packed earth up top, and underneath it a leg caught mid-stride: the thigh swinging forward, the foot planting hard, the last stroke trailing off behind where the ground is still coming loose. Nobody stands like this. You only ever hold this shape when you <radical>run</radical>.

A frame with two uprights driven through it and a pair of bars ruled across the middle, dividing the whole thing into compartments. It is a rack, or a printing block, or a set of pigeonholes — some workshop tool that only exists because somebody had a job for it. Made to be picked up and put to <radical>use</radical>.

Picture a single grain in the middle with husks flying off in every direction — the top strokes spraying up, the bottom strokes kicking down — like a kernel bursting apart the instant it's threshed. That little explosion of scattering pieces is a grain of <radical>rice</radical>.
items.description: 来 is 米 with one extra horizontal laid across the top. Count the horizontal strokes: 米 has one, 来 has two.

items.mnemonic_text: A figure drawn side-on: a head at the top, then a torso thickened out through the middle, and one stroke swinging down and away underneath for the legs. It is a person seen as a shape rather than a face — height, weight, the way they carry themselves. The whole physical <radical>body</radical>.

Picture an old wizard standing tall, his flowing beard streaming down from his chin in a wide fan of strokes that pool at the bottom. That beard has been growing untouched for decades — impossibly, endlessly <radical>long</radical>.

Two uprights with a bar across them and one short stroke floating in the middle of the gap. That stroke is a mouthful being held on the tongue, right between the teeth, and nobody is in a hurry to swallow it. You only hold food in your mouth like that when it is <radical>sweet</radical>.

Picture a person slouched sideways in a chair, their body bent into that leaning top stroke while their legs sprawl out below — mouth cracked wide open in a huge, jaw-stretching yawn, so worn out they <radical>lack</radical> the energy to sit up straight.
items.description: 欠 opens wide at the top and drops into two strokes meeting in a peak, with no horizontal stroke anywhere. 攵 puts a flat horizontal bar under its opening slash. That bar is the whole difference.

items.mnemonic_text: Look at 水 and you'll see a single central stream running straight down, with two smaller trickles splashing off to either side — it's the exact moment a drop hits the surface and sprays outward. That splash frozen mid-air is <radical>water</radical>.

See that little box tucked under a leaning cliff-face? That's the mouth of a cave in the hillside, and the boxy shape sitting at its base is a big rounded stone that rolled down and came to rest there — one solid <radical>stone</radical>.
items.description: 石 and 右 both tuck a small box under a two-stroke top. In 石 that top is a cliff: the horizontal runs along the top and only its left end turns down. In 右 the falling stroke comes first and the horizontal crosses it, so the bar sticks out on both sides.

items.mnemonic_text: An eye up at the top, and beneath it a foot planted flat with the heel dug in and the toes braced against the ground. The eye has seen something and the foot has already answered it, refusing to take one more step forward. Fixed there, staring, immovable: this is <radical>stopping</radical> dead.

A flat stroke over the top and, hanging beneath it, three short strokes curving down and in. It is a hand held palm-down with the fingers already curling under, about to close on something from above. Not a grip — a snatch. What comes down out of the sky like that is a <radical>claw</radical>.

Two uprights standing side by side with a single bar laid straight across both of them. They are holding it up together, level, neither one taking more of the weight than the other. Two arms raised to carry the same load: <radical>two hands</radical>.

See those two identical halves standing side by side, each with a short stroke slanting off and a long stroke dropping straight down? Those are two tall stalks with their leaves flicking out — a little grove of <radical>bamboo</radical>.

A stiff vertical perch holds up four short horizontal bars stacked like ruffled tail feathers, with one square patch of bare skin showing through near the foot where the plumage gave out. It hasn't flown in years and has no plans to start: just an <radical>old bird</radical> gathering dust on its rail.
items.description: This shape shows up as a component inside several taught kanji, always contributing its stacked-feather look rather than standing for a full bird word on its own.

items.mnemonic_text: A tiny hat perches on top, and beneath it one spike drives straight down through three stacked bars like a skewer loaded with peppers. The man holding it stands rigid at the counter, eyes streaming, hat lifting off his head on a column of sweat, insisting nothing here is <radical>spicy</radical>.

Two stray hairs stick up over a flat brow, and beneath them a boxed-in face is craning at the top shelf. It is a giraffe in a business suit, and as it stretches, every shirt button pops off one by one down its telescoping <radical>neck</radical>.

A hooked stroke swings out at the top like a collar snagging on a spinning dry-cleaner's rack. The straight spine drops down, then the last stroke flares sideways into a sleeve that whips loose and smacks the clerk before it settles, hanger and all, into a fresh set of <radical>clothing (left)</radical>.
